issues.description: Constructor parameter ordering for Lecture is inconsistent between the exercise artifacts. The problem statement instructs students to follow the UML diagram for constructor order (problem_statement.md line 20). The UML lists attributes in this order: numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors (problem_statement.md lines 64-68). The solution implementation declares the Lecture constructor with a different parameter order starting with lectureName (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13: Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors)). This mismatch (UML vs. solution) can confuse students about the expected constructor signature and lead to failing tests or incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fixes: (A) Update the solution (and any tests) so the Lecture constructor parameter order matches the UML (numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors), and update the template to provide the same signature; or (B) if the intended order is lectureName first, update the UML and the textual attribute list in problem_statement.md to show that same order and explicitly state the constructor signature. Also update the template instructions to state the exact constructor parameter order to avoid ambiguity.
